thread:
oncall-bot: PAGER: inference-runtime-prod - high error rate detected (>10% 5xx, p95 latency >5s). Paging oncall rotation. Incident ID: INC-20260314-1 :rotating_light:

alex: acked. I’m on it, jumping to dashboard and logs now.

maria: grabbing logs + tail from the edge collectors. any known deploys in last 30m?

lee: no deploys in the window from k8s-deploy. Last model rollout was 2h ago.

alex: impact summary for triage: API rate steady, 2xx down from 98% -> 88%. Affected routes: /v1/generate and /v1/chat. Initial hypothesis: a spike in KV-cache misses increasing backend work.

sam: quick check — are we falling back to larger context models? I see fallback counts ticked up in traces.

maria: pasting a snippet from the edge logs (note: body redaction removed due to sampling):
```
2026-03-14T22:12:42Z edge-collector-3 request_id=abc123 route=/v1/generate status=500 err="runtime: kv-cache miss + OOM"
2026-03-14T22:12:43Z edge-collector-3 request_id=abc124 route=/v1/chat status=502 err="upstream: model variant timeout"
```

alex: running an ad-hoc query against logs-storage for full traces, but I’m only getting header-level logs. bodies are missing for many requests.

jaya: heads-up — I see that fluentd sampling rule was changed in staging config a little while ago and accidentally applied to production via a puppet roll last hour. It reduced 'body' sampling to 5%.

maria: that explains missing request bodies. we can’t reconstruct prompts for root cause without them.

lee: timeline so far: 22:11 error spike begins, 22:12 oncall bot paged, 22:14 sampling change landed (unintended), 22:16 errors escalate. putting that into timeline doc.

alex: hypothesis tracking (in-thread):
H1: sampling change removed bodies -> inability to debug performance regressions quickly (observability gap).
H2: underlying runtime experienced KV-cache churn causing latency, independent of sampling.
H3: a routing change bumped traffic to slower GPU pool -> model timeouts.

sam: evidence: fallback counts + model timeout logs point to H2/H3. missing bodies supports H1.

matt: meantime, mitigation ideas: 1) revert sampling rule to restore body capture (will increase costs) 2) enable temporary higher cache TTL for prefix keys 3) route heavy queries to dedicated pool fallback. Thoughts?

alex: do 1 and 2 in parallel. revert sampling now (maria?), I'll push cache TTL tweak. patching dashboards after revert to show complete traces.

maria: rolling revert of puppet fluentd change now. command: `puppet apply -e "class { 'logging::fluentd': body_sampling => 100 }"`

ops-bot: puppet run queued on 3 nodes. run id: pr-7845.

lee: confirming cache TTL patch: `kubectl patch deployment runtime-service -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","env":[{"name":"KV_CACHE_TTL","value":"600"}]}]}}}}'` will be applied and autoscaling unchanged.

alex: applying cache TTL patch.

maria: revert finished on 3/3 nodes, logs now showing bodies for new requests. pulling earlier tails to see if we can rehydrate traces.

jaya: note — we can’t retroactively capture bodies for already-sampled requests. only new ones will have bodies. sampling window = now.

sam: after revert, 22:20 to 22:30 shows 2xx creeping back to 95%. p95 latency improved by ~900ms. suggests observability change helped diagnosis and mitigation aligned.

lee: I ran an ad-hoc histogram of response times pre/post TTL tweak: 
```
before: p95=5400ms, p99=10800ms
after: p95=4500ms, p99=7200ms
```

alex: still seeing spikes ~22:27 tied to a tiny set of request patterns (long context prompts). might be cache churn.

matt: for the record, I’m opening INC-RCA-20260314 in the RCA board, adding H1/H2/H3 and tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml.

jaya: we also found a dashboard panel that was using `sum(rate(errors[5m]))` but with a downsampling window of 1m in lumberjack which hid the initial uptick. I’ll file a dashboard correction PR.

maria: collecting customer impact notes: two customers reported degraded UX (slower streaming & occasional 502s) between 22:11 and 22:35. I’ve DM'd CSMs for follow-up.

alex: next steps before handoff: 1) confirm no ongoing elevated 5xx for 15m 2) land dashboard PR to surface per-model variant error rates 3) add a retention exception or short-term higher sampling for affected services 4) ensure canary routing ready.

lee: monitoring window clear at 22:45, error rates back to baseline for 20m. will keep watch.

matt: handing off to alex2 (next oncall) in 30m. summary for handoff message (copyable):
- incident: INC-20260314-1, inference-runtime-prod, start 2026-03-14T22:11Z
- root causes under investigation: fluentd sampling rule accidentally applied (observability gap) + possible KV-cache churn causing latency
- mitigations applied: sampling revert, KV_CACHE_TTL increased, dashboard fixes underway
- impact: transient customer-facing errors and latency for ~24 minutes for subset of requests

alex: adding a concrete followup: we need to add a gated test in deployment pipeline to prevent logging sampling flips from promo to prod without a ratified change ID. filing a ticket.

jaya: created ticket TKT-1849 - "prevent fluentd sampling promos" and linked the puppet change.

oncall-bot: Handoff: alex -> alex2 @ 23:15Z. If error rate >3% again, page ENG-SRE.

alex: thanks all. I’ll draft the in-incident RCA timeline and attach logs that have bodies after revert. Please add short notes under H1/H2 with any new evidence.

maria: attaching a small sample of full-body logs (redacted) to the RCA board for 22:20-22:30 window.

sam: quick note: consider adding a lightweight live-sampler that keeps 100% bodies for 10s after any >5% 5xx spike to help future triage. filing FR.

lee: noted. moving to post-incident actions: dashboard PR, sampling policy, TTL default change, canary routing config.

alex: closing the incident thread in Slack; RCA doc will be updated. If anyone sees recurrence, re-open channel or file a new pager. :white_check_mark:
